idiom_name: fan-in goroutine over a result channel + sync.WaitGroup/errgroup
implementation_notes: Go replaces the aggregator object with a goroutine that owns the partial results: fan-out goroutines write into a channel (or into disjoint slots/map entries under a mutex) and sync.WaitGroup or errgroup.Wait() provides the wait-for-all completeness condition, after which the owner merges and forwards the single aggregate downstream. errgroup (golang.org/x/sync/errgroup) adds error propagation and context cancellation so a failed fan-out does not publish, and context.WithTimeout supplies the time-out flavour. The classic buffered collector keyed by correlation id is still required when partials arrive from outside the process (broker, socket) and must be de-duplicated and expired - no Go primitive does that for you.
pitfalls: Loop variables must be captured (i, v := i, v before Go 1.22) or every goroutine writes the same slot.
Writing disjoint slice slots from goroutines is safe, but a shared map or accumulator needs a mutex or a single owner goroutine - the race detector, not the compiler, finds this.
errgroup.Wait returns the first error: right for fail-fast, wrong when partial results must be published anyway, where each goroutine's error has to be collected separately.
